## EVIDENCE SUMMARY

**Cochrane Reviews**

The single Cochrane review supplied (Manfredi et al.) addresses single- versus multi-visit root canal treatment in a general endodontic population and does not stratify or subgroup cracked teeth [[PMID:27905673]]. It therefore offers no direct evidence on cracked tooth prognosis. Its finding of no difference in radiographic success between visit protocols (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.68–1.21) is applicable to standard endodontic cases but cannot be extrapolated to cracked teeth, where the dominant prognostic driver is structural (crack propagation) rather than microbiological. This Cochrane review has also been superseded by a newer 2022 version.

**Level I — RCTs and Systematic Reviews**

None of the 16 Level I reviews and RCTs in this evidence set addresses cracked teeth as a study population or as a prognostic subgroup. The included reviews cover vital pulp therapy in cariously exposed teeth (Cushley et al., Silva et al., Hatipoğlu et al., Pusa et al.) [[PMID:33222178]] [[PMID:37254176]] [[PMID:40886932]] [[PMID:40518287]], regenerative endodontics (Meschi et al.) [[PMID:35579093]], bioceramic versus resin sealers (Zamparini et al.) [[PMID:38606520]], surgical versus non-surgical retreatment (Del Fabbro et al.) [[PMID:27759881]], single- versus two-visit retreatment (Karaoğlan et al.) [[PMID:35488883]], and VPT in traumatic crown/crown-root fractures (Matoug-Elwerfelli et al.) [[PMID:35348216]]. Matoug-Elwerfelli et al. is the closest topical adjacent — it addresses complicated crown and crown-root fractures (which share some structural features with cracks) — but it evaluates vital pulp therapy in traumatised teeth, not RCT prognosis in longitudinally cracked posterior teeth [[PMID:35348216]]. None of these reviews stratifies outcomes by crack extent, depth, or subcrestal propagation.

**Level II — Prospective Studies**

No prospective cohort in the supplied evidence tracks cracked-tooth RCT outcomes by crack extent.

**Level IIIa / IIIb — Retrospective Cohort and Case-Control Studies**

No retrospective cohort or case-control study addressing cracked-tooth prognosis is included in this evidence set. The cracked-tooth prognostic literature (typically Level IIIa cohorts from academic endodontic practices and the AAE registry) is not represented here.
